alternatives.argument: For each k, the event that the kth order statistic is at most a is the finite union over k-subsets J of the events that every coordinate in J is at most a; this proves measurability. The BH rejection set is exactly the indices with P_i<=Rq/m, because if 0<R<m then P_(R)<=Rq/m<P_(R+1), while R=0 and R=m are handled directly. Fix i and let s be the largest k for which the kth remaining value is at most (k+1)q/m. If P_i<=(s+1)q/m, at least s+1 values pass at rank s+1, so R>=s+1; if R>=s+2, deleting P_i from the R values below Rq/m leaves at least R-1 remaining values, making R-1>=s+1 admissible for s, a contradiction. Thus R=s+1 and i is rejected. Conversely, if P_i>(s+1)q/m but i is rejected at R=r, at least r-1 remaining values are <=rq/m, so r-1<=s and r<=s+1; this contradicts P_i<=rq/m. Therefore I_i/(R vee 1)=1{P_i<=(S_i+1)q/m}/(S_i+1) pointwise.

Fix theta and a true-null index i. The local deterministic lemma gives I_i/(R vee 1)=1{P_i<=(S_i+1)q/m}/(S_i+1), where S_i is measurable from the other p-values. Mutual independence makes P_i independent of S_i; because P_i is exactly uniform, for each r=0,...,m-1, P(P_i<=(r+1)q/m,S_i=r)=((r+1)q/m)P(S_i=r). Summing the pointwise identity over the finite partition {S_i=r} yields E[I_i/(R vee 1)]=sum_r [((r+1)q/m)/(r+1)]P(S_i=r)=q/m. Since FDP V/(R vee 1) is the sum of these terms over the m0 true-null indices, finite linearity gives FDR=(m0/m)q<=q. This proves the full result locally under all-m mutual independence and exact true-null uniformity.
